topic: Existing tools and outlook (2024 to Nov 2026)
summary: Tools that write notes are common and increasingly tested; measured time savings are small and depend on the product, while perceived workload often improves. Tools that summarise the whole record are newer: one randomised trial found no time saving, and a closely monitored hospital system still produced about two unsupported claims per summary. Linking each value to its source is becoming a selling point, but most tools link only to a note, transcript or document, and no study was found showing that links reduce errors. Open tools such as LangExtract and LLM-AIx let German researchers try extraction locally, and accuracy must be tested per variable on their own documents. German policy pushes AI documentation and structured research data; PDF findings in the ePA are not planned to reach the research data centre.

findings.claim: In a randomised trial of Epic's AI chart summaries, clinicians reported less task load but saved no charting time, and use declined.
findings.detail: 284 outpatient clinicians, 42 specialties, one academic system, 90 days in 2026. Task load -27.4 on a 0 to 400 scale (CI -49.4 to -5.3). Charting time -1.2 s per encounter (CI -19.0 to 16.6). Interaction fell from 21.5% to 10.5% of summaries. Preprint.
findings.source: A Pragmatic Randomized Trial of an EHR-Integrated Generative AI Chart Summarization Tool for Ambulatory Clinicians, medRxiv (via Sciety)
findings.talk_use: Reality check: an unrequested summary is rarely used; argue for answering specific questions.

findings.claim: In Stanford's record chatbot a summary contained on average 2.33 unsupported claims, and the team plans links from each fact to the record.
findings.detail: 719 summaries sampled Sept to Dec 2025: 0.73 hallucinations and 1.60 inaccuracies each; 50% had none or one. Counted by an automated checker adapted from VeriFact. Errors mainly concerned time order, numbers and attribution.
findings.quote: automatic citations linking each extracted fact to its exact location in the medical record
findings.source: Shah et al., Adoption and Use of LLMs at an Academic Medical Center, arXiv 2602.00074
findings.talk_use: Main argument for a chain of proof: a well-run system makes unsupported claims, and provenance is on its to-do list.

findings.claim: Across five US centres, AI scribes were linked to about 16 minutes less documentation time per 8 patient hours.
findings.detail: 8,581 clinicians, 1,809 adopters, difference in differences. Total EHR time -13.4 min (about 3%); after-hours work unchanged; only 32% used it in at least half of visits. Observational.
findings.source: Rotenstein et al., JAMA 2026, doi 10.1001/jama.2026.2253
findings.talk_use: Counter to claims of an hour saved per day.

findings.claim: In a three-arm trial, one scribe cut note time by 9.5% and another had no significant effect.
findings.detail: 238 physicians, 14 specialties, about 72,000 encounters, 2 months, single centre. The DAX estimate (-1.7%, CI -9.4 to 5.9) was seen only in a search snippet. Occasional clinically significant inaccuracies, one mild safety event.
findings.source: Ambient AI Scribes in Clinical Practice: A Randomized Trial, NEJM AI 2025; read via UCLA Health release
findings.talk_use: Effects depend on the product.

findings.claim: A stepped-wedge trial found 0.36 hours less note time per day and less work exhaustion with an ambient scribe.
findings.detail: 66 volunteer practitioners in one system, 71,487 notes; exhaustion and disengagement -0.44 on a five-point scale. Open label; note quality scored by an LLM; vendor reviewed the manuscript.
findings.source: A Pragmatic Randomized Controlled Trial of Ambient AI to Improve Health Practitioner Well-Being, NEJM AI 2025
findings.talk_use: Positive counterweight to the null results.

findings.claim: Overnight AI drafts of hospital courses were used in 57% of discharges without a significant time saving.
findings.detail: Prospective ward pilot, 384 discharges; 10.7 to 7.8 min (not significant); burnout score 1.75 to 1.20; omissions 25%, inaccuracies 20%, hallucinations 2%. Read in a secondary German summary.
findings.source: Grolleau et al., JAMA Network Open 2026;9(5):e2616556, via IWW CB ChefaerzteBrief
findings.talk_use: Omissions were more common than invented facts, and a source link cannot show what is missing.

findings.claim: AI drafts of hospital courses needed less editing but contained more confabulations than physician drafts.
findings.detail: 100 admissions (study run Dec 2023), 10 residents editing for 3 min each, 8 hospitalists rating. Confabulation rating worse by 0.98 (P=.002); overall quality similar.
findings.source: Small et al., JAMA Network Open 2025;8(8):e2526339
findings.talk_use: Less editing does not mean more correct.

findings.claim: UKE's ARGO drafts discharge letters on premises, and its maker says every statement carries its source.
findings.detail: In use at UKE since Aug 2024; IDMBase also at Schoen Klinik. Vendor statements; no published evaluation found. Declared not a medical device.
findings.source: IDM gGmbH, ARGO and IDMBase product page
findings.talk_use: German example of source linking as a product feature.

findings.claim: Voice documentation by Corti is being rolled out inside ORBIS, without published outcome data.
findings.detail: Partnership July 2025; ambient scribe via ORBIS Speech Assistant started in Germany and was shown at DMEA April 2026. Vendor text gives no clinical results.
findings.source: Corti, Corti and Dedalus are expanding across Europe
findings.talk_use: Shows that the ORBIS vendor's visible AI work starts with creating new notes.

findings.claim: Dedalus and Corti present ORBIS Buddy, a natural-language agent layer for ORBIS with the DACH region first.
findings.detail: Covers retrieval, documentation and order preparation with human confirmation. Analyst blog of unclear sponsorship; no sites, dates or results.
findings.source: Efficiently Connected, Dedalus and Corti Build the Agentic EHR With ORBIS Buddy
findings.talk_use: Q&A: will ORBIS do this itself? Presented, no public evidence found.

findings.claim: An integrator states that Dedalus provides no MCP server for ORBIS, so own LLM tools need HL7 v2, ISiK FHIR or IHE integration.
findings.detail: Marketing page of a third party; read-only access suggested. Not confirmed by Dedalus. Page undated.
findings.quote: Einen MCP-Server stellt Dedalus dafür nicht bereit.
findings.source: innFactory, CompanyGPT integration Dedalus ORBIS
findings.talk_use: Backup for Q&A on technical access; not a main claim.

findings.claim: Microsoft Dragon Copilot has been available in Germany since October 2025 after pilots at five hospitals, without published German outcome numbers in the announcement.
findings.detail: Pilots: Charite, Mannheim, Stuttgart, Hannover, Halle. The quoted time saving comes from a US survey of 879 users of the predecessor product.
findings.source: Microsoft Deutschland press release
findings.talk_use: Announcement versus evidence.

findings.claim: A model trained on synthetic letters was near perfect on synthetic data but weaker for diagnoses and procedures on real letters.
findings.detail: MedGemma 27B fine-tuned on 75,000 synthetic letters from FHIR data of 41,175 cancer patients. Synthetic scores about 0.99 for tumour, lab and medication, 0.84 for diagnosis codes. 30 real letters rated by physicians; metrics differ between the two tests.
findings.number: Real letters: medication 93.0%, tumour 86.1%, diagnoses 78.9%, procedures 61.3%
findings.source: Eryilmaz et al., J Med Internet Res 2026;28:e92413 (University Hospital Essen)
findings.talk_use: Test on your own documents; accuracy differs by variable.

findings.claim: A German hospital pilots on-premise discharge summaries, and the model invented follow-up steps that were missing from the source data.
findings.detail: FHIR data to Mistral Small 3.2, 31 internal medicine patients, zero-shot. JSON input gave better summaries than flat text. Single site, few raters, hospital not named.
findings.quote: this information was not provided in the FHIR source data, often resulting in hallucinated text
findings.source: Medical Summarization in Practice, EACL 2026 Industry Track
findings.talk_use: A template must allow 'not documented' as an answer.

findings.claim: Google's open LangExtract library ties each extracted item to its position in the source text and marks items it cannot locate.
findings.detail: Apache 2.0, works with local models via Ollama. Unlocated items get char_interval None and can be filtered. Not an officially supported Google product; no clinical accuracy benchmark found.
findings.source: Google LangExtract, GitHub
findings.talk_use: Free tool that demonstrates the source-link principle.

findings.claim: LLM-AIx lets non-programmers extract tables from reports on a local server and check them against a gold standard.
findings.detail: TCGA pathology: 87% overall accuracy on 100 reports in about 60 min with Llama 3.1 70B on one 48 GB GPU. Report and output are shown side by side; no link to the exact passage described. Web version is a research prototype, AGPL-3.0.
findings.source: LLM-AIx (medRxiv 2024; npj Precision Oncology 2025) and KatherLab/llmaixweb
findings.talk_use: Practical German starting point for a doctoral project.

findings.claim: A local prototype shows each extracted value with the highlighted sentence in the original PDF, and its study names false reassurance as a risk.
findings.detail: gpt-oss-20b via Ollama; 2 research assistants and 4 experts; qualitative only. A participant preferred blank fields over unsupported values. Highlights can encourage over-skimming.
findings.source: EndoExtract, arXiv 2601.18154
findings.talk_use: Closest published relative of source-linked template filling, including its risk.

findings.claim: In a benchmark of extraction from medical documents, a local model came close to a cloud model, but neither exceeded 80% average F1.
findings.detail: 17 tools reviewed, only one met all criteria. 200 synthetic molecular reports including fax quality. Authors conclude that human oversight is still required.
findings.source: Yu et al., Benchmarking LLM-based Information Extraction Tools for Medical Documents, medRxiv
findings.talk_use: Local costs little accuracy; scan quality matters.

findings.claim: A fully local pipeline for filling case report forms from notes reached a macro-F1 of 0.55 and still ranked second among local entries.
findings.detail: MedGemma-27B, two stages (is it present, then what value), few-shot, shared task 2026, English track.
findings.source: sebis at CRF Filling 2026, arXiv 2606.13082
findings.talk_use: Counter-evidence: form filling is not solved.

findings.claim: An agent reviewing long myeloma records slightly beat simple retrieval, but its errors were more often serious than disagreements between experts.
findings.detail: 811 patients, 44,962 documents, 469 patient-question pairs. 79.6% agreement vs about 75% for RAG. Error rate 12.2% vs expert disagreement 13.6%. Retrospective.
findings.talk_use: Outlook on agents with a sober second half.

findings.claim: From 2027 ePA data for research are planned to be structured only, starting with the medication list; PDF findings will not be passed on.
findings.detail: Physician association summary of the gematik schedule. Keyword full-text search in the ePA is planned stepwise from Q1 2027. Dates have moved before.
findings.quote: Befunddaten im PDFFormat, die in die ePA eingestellt wurden, werden hingegen nicht an das FDZ weitergegeben.
findings.source: KVB FORUM 3-4/2026, ePA-Ausbaustufen
findings.talk_use: Closing argument: documents stay behind, data travel.

findings.claim: Germany's 2026 strategy wants more than 70% of care facilities to use AI-supported documentation actively in 2028.
findings.detail: Goal in the updated digital strategy (Feb 2026); no baseline found. Also EHDS connection of data infrastructures by end of 2028 and AI test environments.
findings.quote: mehr als 70 Prozent der Einrichtungen sollen diese 2028 aktiv nutzen
findings.source: BMG, Weiterentwicklung der Digitalisierungsstrategie
findings.talk_use: Political direction; pair with the evidence on small effects.

findings.claim: In 2026, 48% of German practices use AI, while almost two thirds still communicate with hospitals mostly on paper.
findings.detail: About 2,300 physicians and psychotherapists. Documentation use 13%. Only 20% receive electronic discharge letters; 3% of ePA documents come from hospitals.
findings.source: KBV PraxisBarometer 2026
findings.talk_use: Fresh status quo contrast: AI and paper side by side.

findings.claim: Half of surveyed German doctors use private AI tools such as ChatGPT for professional research and 28% for documentation.
findings.detail: YouGov for Doctolib, 204 doctors, July to Aug 2025. Vendor with an interest; does not measure entry of patient data.
findings.source: Doctolib Digital Health Report 2026
findings.talk_use: Why hospitals need an approved alternative.

findings.claim: In the USA 81% of physicians use AI professionally, and 88% cite possible skill loss as a concern.
findings.detail: 1,692 physicians, Jan to Feb 2026; 38% in 2023. Read in the ASCO Post, not in the AMA report.
findings.source: AMA 2026 Physician Survey on Augmented Intelligence, via The ASCO Post
findings.talk_use: International comparison and deskilling question.

findings.claim: AI-written summary notes in the record modestly degrade what other AI systems later write, and injected over-diagnoses reappear unnoticed by standard metrics.
findings.detail: Seven reader models from four families, ML4H 2026 Findings.
findings.source: AI in the Clinical Documentation Loop, arXiv 2611.10601
findings.talk_use: Risk slide: link to the original document, not to an AI summary of it.

caveats: Many German tool statements come from vendors or press; no published evaluation of ARGO, ORBIS Buddy or the Corti integration was found.
Several key 2026 studies are preprints or were read only as abstracts.
ChatEHR error counts come from an automated checker.
The UCLA DAX figure was seen only in a search snippet.

WebFetch returns model-made summaries of pages; check numbers and quotes against the original before printing. PDFs marked full text were text-extracted and read in the relevant passages, not cover to cover.
uniGPT's wording on sensitive data does not clear patient data; its page lists old models.
The advantage of source-linked template filling over summaries is an inference; no head-to-head study was found.
gaps: Search budget ran out: Oracle Health, Google Vertex, AWS HealthScribe, John Snow Labs, Mendel, Averbis, Tiplu, ID Berlin, Recare, Noa, Tandem, Heidi, REDCap AI, Kaapana, Docling, FHIR MCP, gematik AI plans and deskilling studies not researched.
No 2026 survey on LLM use by German hospital doctors found.
No study found on how often clinicians open source links.
